Generate a conventional commit message with a subject line AND a multi-line body describing the changes.

Output format (strictly two parts, separated by a blank line):

    <type>(<scope>): <subject>
    <BLANK LINE>
    <body line 1>
    <body line 2>
    <body line 3>

SUBJECT RULES:
- Format: type(scope) description
- Max 72 characters
- Types: feat, fix, docs, style, refactor, test, chore, perf, ci, build, revert
- Description must reflect the actual code changes

BODY RULES:
- Wrap at 72 characters per line
- Use bullet points (start each line with "- ")
- Each bullet explains ONE specific change: what was changed and why
- Be concrete: name the function, file, or behavior affected
- 3-5 bullets is the right size
- Focus on intent, not mechanics

OUTPUT RULES:
- Output ONLY the commit message (subject + blank line + body)
- NEVER use backticks, code fences, or markdown formatting around the message
- Do NOT include "[skip ci]" or any other trailer
- The trailer is added automatically by the workflow

INPUT:

CURRENT MESSAGE: __CURRENT_MSG__
CHANGED FILES (__FILE_COUNT__):
__CHANGED_FILES__

CODE DIFF (added lines only):
__DIFF_CONTENT__
